t: This is St Mary on Paddington Green, an Anglican church now standing at the junction of Edgware Road and Harrow Road, seen by tens of thousands of motorists every day from the Westway. Several notable people are buried in its churchyard. Sarah Siddons, the Welsh actress, was the best-known tragedienne of the eighteenth century, and the critic William Hazlitt called her tragedy personified. The poet Stephen Spender is buried here, and so is the popular historian John Julius Norwich. The landscape painter George Barret the Younger and the engraver James Mason also lie here.
